findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on I/O Result is forbidden
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path panics the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, _> and propagate the I/O error with ? or match

findings.problem: load_sessions performs fs I/O and println! logging inside the same function that should be pure functional core
findings.failure_mode: core logic cannot be unit-tested without filesystem, logging leaks into pure computation, and side effects are not explicit at boundaries
findings.fix: split into a shell function that handles fs::read_to_string and println!, and a pure core fn parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden side effect (stdout I/O) inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: side-effect leaks into pure data processing, breaks testability, and logging is not a first-class action at the shell boundary
findings.fix: remove println! from core path; if logging is needed, return a diagnostic struct from the shell layer

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with zero commas panics with IndexOutOfPanic
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and handle None with map_err or explicit error return

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with zero commas panics with IndexOutOfPanic
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and handle None with map_err or explicit error return

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with only one comma panics with IndexOutOfPanic
findings.fix: use parts.get(1) and handle None with map_err or explicit error return

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on parse Result is forbidden
findings.failure_mode: non-numeric value in CSV panics instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(...)) or ? operator in a Result-returning function

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy cast from u32 to u16 using `as` is forbidden
findings.failure_mode: values > 65535 silently truncate, producing incorrect data without any error signal

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() — collects all split parts into a Vec when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation for every line, and splits on ALL commas even if the grammar only expects one separator
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to extract name and value parts in a single bounded operation, then trim and parse each

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity pre-allocation on the return Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: unbounded reallocation as records are pushed, especially wasteful for large files
findings.fix: accept a line count hint or use try_reserve with checked capacity computation in the shell layer

findings.failure_mode: performance claims about file loading and parsing cannot be verified or measured
findings.fix: add a criterion or miniserde benchmark measuring file load latency, allocation count, and throughput
